newsitem.title: UK: Reed H1 growth to be slowed by strong stg.
newsitem.headline: Reed H1 growth to be slowed by strong stg.

text.p: Good underlying growth from Reed Elsevier will be tempered by the effects of strong sterling when the Anglo-Dutch publishing group reports first-half results on Thursday, analysts said.
Analysts polled by Reuters in London forecast pre-tax profits of 411-445 million stg, against 416 million stg a year ago. Interim dividend is expected to come in between 4.35 and 4.65p.
Reed Elsevier co-chairman Nigel Stapleton said in March the strong pound could drag down headline earnings by five percent this year and sterling has continued to gain since then.
Earnings figures for the combined businesses of the company are expressed in sterling and analysts said the currency impact could be as high as nine percent in the first half.

Reed Elsvier is, however, thought to be pursuing a sound strategy, having sold many of its consumer businesses to focus on the provision of information in fields such as science, business and the legal professions, analysts said.
It has made three sizeable acquisitions in the U.S. this year, buying trade magazine publisher Chilton Business Group from Walt Disney Co's ABC for $447 million in June.

Earlier this year Reed Elsevier bought 40 U.S. law publications from Thomson Corp and its science publishing division bought MDL Information Systems Inc for $320 million. MDL's systems help customers in the chemical, pharmaceutical and bio-tech industries to manage and use information.
